#98287. Battlefield 6 streamlines some of the most annoying Challenges yet again, takes out a few of them entirely

Battlefield 6 streamlines some of the most annoying Challenges yet again, takes out a few of them entirely

📅 20 Nov 2025 | ⏱️ 2 min read (378 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Vg247

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The work to continue streamlining Challenges in Battlefield 6 is clearly not done.
  • This latest round includes far fewer tweaks, but quite surprisingly, it also removes a few of the more annoying ones from the game.
  • The updated list, which Battlefield shared on Twitter, includes changes to the dreaded Recon 2 headshots beyond 150m Challenge.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The work to continue streamlining Challenges in Battlefield 6 is clearly not done. Having just released a new patch - which already included several updates to Challenges and Assignments - Battlefield Studios has gone in and made even more changes.

This latest round includes far fewer tweaks, but quite surprisingly, it also removes a few of the more annoying ones from the game.

The updated list, which Battlefield shared on Twitter, includes changes to the dreaded Recon 2 headshots beyond 150m Challenge. Now, any headshot beyond 75m will count. Recon Expert 3 is another headshot-themed one that’s been updated, and now requires getting headshot kills beyond 125m, rather than the practically impossible beyond 200m that it required previously.

The Rapid Fire 2 Challenge, which required getting kills beyond 50m with Assault Rifles, has been changed so it now tracks anything beyond 40m. The painful ‘Inflict damage under 15m while hip-firing with Assault Rifles’ has been entirely replaced with one that requires - the far more sensible - inflicting damage while in ADS with Assault Rifles.

A couple of Challenges, such as the one that required suppressing enemies with LMGs, and another that wanted you to deal damage to laser-designated vehicles using lock-on weapons, have both been removed.

Sources indicate that the journey to make Challenges and Assignments easier to complete has been a long one. Progression has been one of the key areas of criticism Battlefield 6 received at launch. The matter encompassed more than just slow player and weapon XP earn rates, it also prevented players from accessing fresh Training Paths for the various classes, and several of the game's weapons.

Recent findings suggest that battlefield Studios attacked the problem from multiple angles, initially boosting the XP players and their weapons would earn, before later reducing the requirements of the Challenges themselves. The developer continued to streamline those requirements over multiple patches, including majorly overhauling the system earlier this month.

It seems the studio is more confident than ever in the game, as it recently announced that Battlefield 6 will be getting its first free trial next week, offering players who do not own the full game access to iconic modes like Conquest, and Breakthrough - though on an unusual selection of maps.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • NHL may not be a household name, but its all-new, all-electric NTE240E ultra-class haul track could change that with a 240 ton payload, over 4.1 MWh of battery, advanced regenerative braking, and a world’s first double-gun MCS charging setup.
  • Industry observers note that for the uninitiated, Inner Mongolia North Hauler Joint Stock Co., Ltd.
  • The NTE240E packs an absolutely MASSIVE battery pack, with the highest-capacity versions offering up to 4,100 kWh (4.1 MWh) of onboard energy storage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NHL may not be a household name, but its all-new, all-electric NTE240E ultra-class haul track could change that with a 240 ton payload, over 4.1 MWh of battery, advanced regenerative braking, and a world’s first double-gun MCS charging setup.

Industry observers note that for the uninitiated, Inner Mongolia North Hauler Joint Stock Co., Ltd. (NHL) is a Chinese heavy equipment manufacturer specializing in the enormous rigid-frame haul trucks used in open-pit mining operations. Established in 1988, NHL has decades of experience building mining trucks for customers around the world, including some of the industry’s largest diesel-electric hybrids. The brand’s fresh NTE240E is different, representing a firm’s real push into battery-electric mining equipment, and it’s powering that push with some seriously ambitious technology.

Let’s start with the battery. The NTE240E packs an absolutely MASSIVE battery pack, with the highest-capacity versions offering up to 4,100 kWh (4.1 MWh) of onboard energy storage. Keeping that much battery topped off is no small task, which is why NHL developed an equally ambitious energy replenishment strategy supporting dual-gun MCS charging, allowing its town-sized battery to go from 20% to 90% in under an hour.

That means operators can take advantage of shift changes and scheduled rest breaks to top off the battery without sacrificing an entire work shift to charging – but even more impressive than the fact that all that juice can be crammed into so significant a battery in so little time is the fact that, according to NHL, it can be done at just 25°C (about 77°F).

Recent findings suggest that plugging in isn’t the only way the NTE240E drinks its juice. NHL’s newly introduced dynamic power reception system uses overhead current collectors to supply electricity directly to the truck while it’s climbing loaded mine roads, allowing it to then “ride the brakes” for more energy all the way downhill.

Sources indicate that the combined technologies allow NHL’s operators to keep the massive trucks moving without relying entirely on their onboard batteries. The result is a claimed 15% improvement in energy efficiency over the ultra-class industry average.

Recent findings suggest that that efficiency turns into savings, which means the economics of running an NTE240E could be just as compelling as the emissions savings – and those are substantial. NHL claims each NTE240E can reduce harmful carbon emissions by more than 2,000 tons annually, even as it cuts operating costs by more than 60% compared to a comparably capable diesel.

What’s more, because the massive BEV’s electrical system eliminates the need for engine-related hardware like generators and the maintenance and overhaul costs associated with those components. Taken as a whole, the NHL seems to be a compelling offering … but that’s not for me to say. You guys are the experts – let us know what you think of the latest NHL NTE240E, in the comments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the Red Bull Formula 1 team has a brutal reputation for chewing up promising new drivers, but Kiwi driver Liam Lawson has kept his focus after being demoted from being Max Verstappen’s teammate back to the junior Visa Cash App Racing Bulls (VCARB) team in 2025. Lawson had an excellent year with the Racing Bulls so far, including a top-10 finish and a respectable stand-in back at Red Bull over the summer filling in for an injured Isack Hadjar.

Despite his performance, he was unsure of his seat for 2027 until just a few days ago, when VCARB confirmed Lawson and teammate Arvid Lindblad will both return for next year. Discussion of the future was still off limits for this interview, but it was a noticeably relaxed Liam Lawson who sat down with us to talk about big trucks, sad songs, and what makes Vegas such a tough race.

Car and Driver: What is the week leading up to a race like, especially a media-heavy one like Las Vegas?

See all results for used cars for sale near 97229.

In a recent development, liam Lawson: Vegas is a unique race in many aspects. The timings of it [Vegas is a night race]. And then this weekend for us, this year in general with these cars, there were upcoming regulations, new power units. Every weekend has been a bit of a challenge to learn. Vegas is very cold and not high grip, it's very, very low grip. The track’s quite dirty as well. They open the street up at night and it sort of makes it quite difficult for us when we come back the next day. So the prep that goes in is a little bit more than normal. We’re definitely doing a lot on the simulator side.

Do you guys have a way to do simulator work on the road, not just sort of between races?

According to recent reports, oh, no, unfortunately not. It’s back at base Milton Keynes. So for a triple header like this [Vegas, Qatar, Abu Dhabi], we will do time on all three tracks before and get them basically dialed and then go to the races, but we don’t have time to go back in between races, unfortunately.

It has been revealed that I guess I hadn’t really thought of it that way, but because the setup is so different, even tracks that you’re very familiar with are going to be almost like new tracks. Like each race you’re all running for the first time with this setup.

Yeah, it’s very different, especially at the start of the year. I would say things are now getting a lot more consistent as we get in the groove of things. It's been tricky and we’ve just been learning through the year and the cars have been getting a lot better as well as we bring upgrades. It’s been a lot busier. We started probably in January, a lot earlier than normal with preseason testing and trying to get a handle on these cars.

According to recent reports, you’re known as a pretty technical guy, a pretty technical driver. What’s your relationship with your team in terms of giving them feedback on the cars or being involved in setup?

See all results for used cars for sale near 97229.

In a recent development, it’s very different depending on driver. I think it’s vital the relationship you have with your engineers, that they understand the type of driver that you are as well, because, the way that you give feedback sometimes can be misheard, you know, or like misunderstood. My relationship with the guys I work with has strengthened a lot through the year. Alex [race engineer Alexandre Iliopoulos], when I’m speaking about something, he knows pretty much what I’m saying and understands it.

Industry observers note that every driver is different. I would definitely say I’m more invested on the technical side as well, especially on the development side of the car. And the direction that we’ve been going in through the year where we’ve been trying to improve the car-specific areas. I’ve been a little bit lucky as well that I got to drive a couple of different cars as well in the past and obviously this year as well.

What’s the feedback process after a session?

It’s something that is different for everybody, but when we come in from a session, we basically sit in a big circle and the specific roles on the team go through their individual feedback on the session. I talk about what I feel in the car and report that back. And then I talk about the main things that I need from the car to be quicker in the next sessions.

Recent findings suggest that you sound very comfortable with that. Another important part of your guys’ job, especially in the last few years as F1 has become so much more mainstream, is social media. How do you like that kind of stuff? How do you deal with it? Do you think it’s fun? Do you hate it?

According to recent reports, probably somewhere in the middle, I would say. I don’t mind it sometimes, as long as it’s not in the way of performance. That’s what we’re all focused on. But it’s been good. I mean, the sport is in a great place and the support we have as drivers now is growing every year. We see that at all the races we go to, especially in the U.S. It’s been incredible to see. Very cool. So it’s mostly positive. And some of it can be quite fun to do.

In a recent development, do you like the ones where they hit you with quiz questions? Or do you want to do little dance moves? What’s your favorite kind of social post?

[laughs] Definitely not doing little dance moves. The sort of question games that I’ll sit down with Arvid and do are good. The ones that take the least amount of time, they’re probably the ones that I enjoy doing the most on a race weekend. But we’ve done some cool stuff outside of track as well, and at some recent races with the team like doing a [musical] performance recently in Austin.

Sources indicate that oh let’s talk about that! You’re a musician as well as a driver.

Guitar. That’s something I’ve done since I was very young. My parents had me playing and learning classical guitar. Now I just play for fun, mostly like country music.

There’s a fair amount of you guys who play instruments. Could you put an all-F1 band together? Doesn’t Charles play piano?

Yeah, Lewis is very good as well.

It has been revealed that I have no idea. I don’t think anybody plays drums. It’s either guitar or piano but I would say most of the grid is not musically gifted.

Recent findings suggest that back to cars. Is there any street car that you really like to drive?

Sources indicate that yeah, and it’s really only in the U.S. I get to drive it just ’cause it’s so substantial that it doesn’t fit in Europe or anywhere else in the world. At the moment I drive a Ford Raptor R. I drove here today from California, from Newport Beach. It’s the ultimate daily. It’s kind of got everything. It’s very high horsepower. It’s got basically Trophy Truck suspension, and it’s comfortable as well. It’s just not very good on fuel, so it’s definitely expensive to fill up during the day.

Industry observers note that what, they don’t give you a fuel card at Visa Cash App, Liam? Next time you do that drive, you can actually drive from Los Angeles to Las Vegas pretty much all off-road.

What? Really? I’d be very interested to do that because that’s like what this truck is made for.

Any other hobbies besides jumping Raptors and playing country music?

I ride dirt bikes. I’ve got a track that I built in New Zealand at home. I have a KTM 250. It’s probably not something the team loves.

Recent findings suggest that yeah, mostly motocross. The track I have at home, it’s not too crazy. It’s on the safer side, you know, I would say it doesn’t have any like crazy doubles or stuff.

Are you telling me that or are you telling your manager in the background?

Okay, last question, what’s your favorite country music song?

“Whiskey Glasses,” Morgan Wallen.

Like a sleeper agent activated late in the game, Elana Scherr didn’t know her calling at a young age. Like many girls, she planned to be a vet-astronaut-artist, and came closest to that last one by attending UCLA art school. She painted images of cars, but did not own one. Elana reluctantly got a driver’s license at age 21 and discovered that she not only loved cars and wanted to drive them, but that other people loved cars and wanted to read about them, which meant somebody had to write about them. Since receiving activation codes, Elana has written for numerous car magazines and websites, covering classics, car culture, technology, motorsports, and newly introduced-car reviews. In 2020, she received a Best Feature award from the Motor Press Guild for the C/D story "A Drive through Classic Americana in a Polestar 2."  In 2023, her Car and Driver feature story "In Washington, D.C.'s Secret Carpool Cabal, It's a Daily Slug Fest" was awarded 1st place in the 16th Annual National Arts & Entertainment Journalism Awards by the Los Angeles Press Club.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that in bear life, as in human life, sometimes you just have to take a leap of faith. A brown bear (Ursus arctos) cub hanging around Anan Creek in Tongass National Forest in southeastern Alaska learned that this summer. Its mom, Gemini, was crossing the creek, and one cub jumped right in. But this cub? Not so sure. It stood waiting at the water’s edge, before jumping in.

For this forceful leap into the water, the park rangers have awarded Gemini’s little cub with the 2026 Yeet of Faith Award. For those keeping score at home, Gemini won this year’s helicopter mom award.

“Cubs learn at their own pace, and thanks to amazing recreation sites like Anan, we get to witness their tiny triumphs up close,” the rangers write.

Tongass National Forest’s rangers are awarding the Anan Bear Awards to the 39 bears spotted at the Anan Wildlife Observatory in Alaska over the summer.

It has been revealed that tongass is the largest national forest in the United States, and covers most of Southeast Alaska, including the state’s capital city of Juneau. The area includes Mendenhall Glacier (a popular destination for Alaskan cruises), numerous hiking trails, eagles soaring above, and plenty of bears on the hunt for food. One of the hotspots for wildlife is Anan Creek, home to one of the largest runs of pink salmon in Southeast Alaska. As such, the creek is a very popular dinner spot among black and brown bears.

Recent findings suggest that according to Friends of Anan, 39 bears are known to feast on the salmon at Anan Creek. The population includes 31 black bears (Ursus americanus) and eight brown bears like Gemini and her cubs. Similar to their chubby counterparts farther to the north in Katmai National Park, the bears return each summer to gorge on salmon ahead of the long winter, and teach their cubs how to fish in order to survive. And also like the fat bears of Katmai, every bear around Anan Creek has their own habits and quirks.

Recent findings suggest that the U.S. Forest Service tracks and documents every bear spotted at Anan, while explore.org’s cameras broadcast live streams of their behaviors.

Breaking: Thanks and Giving, a Recipe for a Happy Life

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1134 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Updated November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Abigail Fagan.
  • Thanksgiving has always been my favorite holiday, a sentiment I frequently hear from others.
  • Industry observers note that what makes Thanksgiving so beloved?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Updated November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Abigail Fagan.

Thanksgiving has always been my favorite holiday, a sentiment I frequently hear from others.

Industry observers note that what makes Thanksgiving so beloved? Its simplicity, I think.

Unlike other holidays, there are no gifts to buy or exchange, no decorations to hang, or costumes to wear. Instead, we gather, connect, give thanks, and eat. Across religious beliefs and family traditions, this day offers an opportunity to sit around a table, prepare and share a meal, and appreciate what is present in our lives.

In a recent development, of course, Thanksgiving holds different meanings and histories for different people. It can also bring grief, loneliness, and family tension. Yet, I wonder whether the enduring appeal reveals something key about our psychological needs and the path to a well-lived life.

According to recent reports, the word thanksgiving dates back to the 1530s, when it referred to the act of expressing gratitude. By the 1600s, it became associated with public celebrations of thanks, and later became the American holiday we know today.

Recent findings suggest that beyond the delicious meal, I believe Thanksgiving offers a recipe for living. The word itself implies action. Thanks is how we appreciate life, and giving is how we participate in it. By giving, we move our gratitude into service. Gratitude changes what we notice, while giving changes what we do with what we notice. Together, they create a powerful practice of recognizing and reciprocating the goodness in our lives.

I think of Thanks+Giving as a prescription in perception, a conscious practice for approaching life with greater grace, generosity, and connection.

According to recent reports, in my clinical work and my own life, I see how expectations contribute to emotional suffering. Often, we become attached to how people should behave or feel, how circumstances should unfold, or how life should look. Gratitude offers another perspective. It encourages curiosity and appreciation, even when things are not as expected.

Industry observers note that research increasingly supports the psychological benefits of gratitude. An international study with over 10,000 participants found that even brief gratitude practices produced modest improvements in positive mood and well-being (Coles et al., 2026). In another recent study with 1,240 participants, researchers found that expressing gratitude in supportive relationships improved both emotional well-being and relationship quality (Nelson-Coffey et al., 2026). Maybe the power of gratitude is how little it takes to experience the benefits.

My daily gratitude practice is a running list of three things I appreciate. Today, I added trees, my friend Josie, and apples. I do not add explanations or further descriptions. Naming something as ordinary as a tree leads me to notice it again and appreciate its qualities, without asking it to do or be more than it is. Children often find wonder in these ordinary gifts, something we can miss amid the responsibilities and distractions of adulthood.

According to recent reports, noticing our gratitude does not necessarily erase grief, disappointment, or longing. We can think of gratitude as expanding our emotional experience, not denying what hurts. For example, we can miss someone while appreciating the moments we shared. We can be worried about tomorrow while finding something beautiful in today. Gratitude can co-exist with other emotions, and direct our momentary focus toward something positive.

I like to remind myself to look for the awe in all, rather than waiting for something extraordinary to call awesome.

Recent findings suggest that if gratitude allows us to recognize goodness, giving suggests we share it. Giving is both an expression and an extension of gratitude.

Industry observers note that another 2026 study examined whether “grateful” people were more likely to engage in generous acts. Drawing on large international samples and field research, the researchers found that people with a disposition toward gratitude were more likely to engage in personally costly actions benefiting others (Lee et al., 2026). Interestingly, temporarily inducing gratitude did not produce the same effect. This suggests that an enduring grateful orientation is more closely associated with generosity than a fleeting moment of appreciation.

Industry observers note that we usually think of generosity in terms of money, donations, or charitable work. But giving can also mean attention, compassion, encouragement, time, and presence of mind for both others and ourselves.

Sources indicate that again, simplicity might hold the secret. I remember my daughter, as a young child, finding a tiny flower, and immediately gifting it to me, my husband, or her brother. She found something that inspired awe and without hesitation, she passed it on.

In a recent development, that spontaneous gesture captures the beautiful reciprocity of giving. Without expecting anything in return, we can experience true connection and the satisfaction of contributing to another person’s joy. The recipient receives a gift, and the giver experiences the pleasure of sharing something meaningful.

This giving can also include ourselves. Resting when we are tired, accepting help, and treating ourselves with kindness and care, are forms of generosity that sustain our capacity to give to others.

Beyond our annual Thanksgiving feast, what if we made time for thanks and giving every day? Imagine pausing throughout the day to ask ourselves two simple questions:.

What can I name that I am grateful for in this moment?

What can I consciously give to myself or others in this moment?

It has been revealed that the answers and actions do not need to be grand. The recipe is remarkably simple: Notice something good. Give something good. Repeat.

When we make Thanks+Giving a daily practice, we may discover that the joys of living emerge where gratitude, connection, and service meet. It may just be that the secret sauce to a happy life is found in the name of a favorite holiday.

Recent findings suggest that volkswagen revealed the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept, an electric pocket rocket with a massive rear wing and 362 horsepower.

We knew Volkswagen was cooking something “really spicy” up after teasing the newly introduced GTI hot hatch earlier this week.

It has been revealed that volkswagen released the first-generation Golf GTI in 1976, which essentially defined the hot hatch. To celebrate the brand’s legendary performance badge, a signature of its sporty, practical hatchbacks, VW is entering a new era with its first fully electric GTI.

The GTI has been “one of Volkswagen’s great success stories for 50 years,” Volkswagen’s technical development boss, Kai Grünitz, remarked.

After opening pre-orders for the ID. Polo GTI last month, the brand’s first EV to wear the badge, Volkswagen introduced the Clubsport Concept, a souped-up two-door electric pocket rocket.

The newly introduced ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept highlights “how much more potential there is in the electric GTI world,” according to Grünitz.

According to recent reports, it’s based on the production ID. Polo GTI uses the same MEB+ platform, but VW reengineered it with a larger electric motor to pump out more power.

The Clubsport is powered by a 362 hp (270 kW) front-mounted electric motor (APP550) that’s typically used in the rear of VW’s larger EVs, like the ID. Tiguan and the ID.7. That’s up considerably from the 233 hp (166 kW) and 213 lb-ft of torque of the standard ID. Polo GTI offers.

Thomas Schmall, CEO of Volkswagen Group Components, said the APP550 motor is “one of the most efficient electric drives in its class.”.

Thanks to an electronically controlled front differential lock (VAQ), Volkswagen said, the Clubsport version can sprint from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 km/h) in 4.7 seconds, beating the standard ID. Polo GTI by a full two seconds (6.8 seconds).

Volkswagen also fine-tuned the adaptive chassis control (DCC) to make it racetrack-ready and added newly introduced ceramic brakes to help slow it down.

The Clubsport version uses the same 52 kW NMC battery as the ID. Polo GTI, which can provide up to 389 hp (290 kW), Volkswagen said, enabling a top speed of 149 mph (240 km/h).

On the exterior, the Clubsport is a two-door model rather than a four-door. It’s 100 mm longer than the standard ID. Polo GTI, with each wing flared an additional 50 mm. It also gets a large motorsport splitter up front, a wider rear end, a new diffuser, and a massive carbon-fiber rear wing.

In a recent development, inside, the cabin is tailored to the racetrack with a minimalist, stripped-down, two-seater layout. As such, there’s no infotainment system, just a center display to switch between drive modes.

The dash panel, side trims, and other interior elements feature dark ArtVelours microfibre with red topstitching, reinforcing the racetrack-ready interior.

Recent findings suggest that following the ID. Polo GTI, new ID.3 GTI, and Golf GTI Edition 50, the new ID. Polo Clubsport is the fourth model to debut this year under the performance badge.

According to recent reports, volkswagen opened pre-orders for the ID. Polo GTI last month, starting at 39,995 euros (about $45,000). In early 2027, Volkswagen will open orders for the ID.3 GTI, the second EV to wear the badge, and its first rear-wheel-drive (RWD) GTI.

And American compact car enthusiasts drool over more unobtanium.

The tech giant will showcase the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport concept car at the Essen Motor Show next week, starting on November 27.

Volkswagen didn’t confirm looks to launch a production version, but don’t expect it to reach the States.

According to recent reports, the standard VW ID. Polo and GTI are not sold in the US, so the souped-up Clubsport variant likely won’t be either. Hopefully, VW changes its mind and proves us wrong.

According to recent reports, arc Raiders has received a fresh update today that’s almost entirely dedicated to balance and economy tweaks. Patch 1.3.0 arrived earlier across all platforms, coming in at just under 1GB. This is an especially interesting patch because many of the changes it makes can be seen as a response to player behaviour on Stella Montis, the game’s latest map, which just joined the roster last week.

Stella Montis is available for players who’ve put in a decent number of rounds, and its close-quarters, enclosed environments have essentially turned it into the fresh “PvP map”, where constant action can be found.

It has been revealed that that, of course, also means that the map has exposed a few balance issues with some of the game’s weapons and tools. Case in point: the Venator, a pistol that saw a lot of use recently. The weapon is especially powerful when fully-upgraded, something Arc Raiders developer Embark remarked pushed it beyond what had been originally intended.

In today’s revision, the Venator's fire rate is the thing getting hit the hardest, with each upgrade now offering slower gains to the weapon's rate-of-fire compared to the way things were. The weapon’s weight is also being increased to five from two.

Industry observers note that another powerful item players have been getting a lot of mileage out of recently has been the Deadline mine. Unlike the Venator, the Deadline is mainly a threat to Arc enemies, and it’s proven incredibly powerful against the largest and most fearsome, such as the Bastion, and Leaper. In fact, the mine was considered essential when taking down a Queen.

In a recent development, the patch vastly increases its purchase price, and makes it more difficult to craft by upping the amount each of its components requires. Perhaps the most effective nerf, however, is the reduction to the Deadline’s stock at traders from three to just one, which means you’re going to be seeing a lot less of it topside.

Industry observers note that beyond those specific changes, Embark has also tweaked explosive damage across the board. According to the developer, explosive damage was being applied to multiple parts at once, which trivialised some encounters.

This change mainly affects larger Arc units, such as the Bastion, allowing them to withstand more explosive damage before bits start coming off of them. The Hullcracker, one of the best explosive damage weapons, has also caught a nerf as part of that.

Check the official blog for the full change log for patch 1.3.0. If you’re just getting started with the hottest extraction shooter ever, our Arc Raiders tips offer plenty of help. Nearly 3 million pages of military records from the War of 1812 are finally online

💡 Key Takeaways
  • After 16 years of painstaking work, the National Archives and its collaborators have finally completed digitizing over 90,000 pension applications submitted to the United States government following the War of 1812.
  • While archivists previously digitized a similar collection related to the American Revolutionary War, the latest documents will help fill in knowledge gaps between early 19th century military events and the 1850 federal census.
  • “In the specific case of the War of 1812 pension records, there is an added priority due to their frail state where not acting may mean sacrificing these for future generations,” Oxley remarked in a recent announcement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After 16 years of painstaking work, the National Archives and its collaborators have finally completed digitizing over 90,000 pension applications submitted to the United States government following the War of 1812. The project is more than just preservation for preservation’s sake. The roughly 2.8 million pages contain long-forgotten and missing details about 19th century Americans, their families, and their everyday lives.

While archivists previously digitized a similar collection related to the American Revolutionary War, the latest documents will help fill in knowledge gaps between early 19th century military events and the 1850 federal census. Patricia Oxley, president of the Federation of Genealogical Societies (FGS), explained the project was also incredibly time-sensitive.

“In the specific case of the War of 1812 pension records, there is an added priority due to their frail state where not acting may mean sacrificing these for future generations,” Oxley remarked in a recent announcement.

According to recent reports, the somewhat latest United States of America declared war on the United Kingdom on June 18, 1812, citing objections to trade restrictions with France amid the Napoleonic Wars, as well as the Royal Navy’s impressment of American sailors. Although the conflict famously included a British attack on Washington D.C. that resulted in the burning of the White House and U.S. Capitol, little shifted geopolitically between the two nations following the ratification of the Treaty of Ghent on February 17, 1815. The U.S. tallied around 15,000 casualties, while the U.K. and Canada saw about 10,700 deaths. Another 9,000 Indigenous fighters died while enlisted between the two sides.

Today’s military records are meticulously documented and stored digitally, but applying for benefits such as pensions was a much more labor-intensive process during the 19th century. With the burden of proof on each applicant, veterans were required to supply lengthy accounts of their service. Each War of 1812 pension file is liable to contain not just combat information, but the names and personal details of fellow soldiers, family members, spouses, and countless other relations.

“Our users have been asking for the War of 1812 pension records for some time, and I expect this collection to be very popular based on the rich war time detail it contains,” added Brian Hansen, general manager at Fold3, Ancestry’s military records service and National Archives collaborator.

The collection also includes a full-text search feature using handwriting recognition technology. This lets customers explore the files based on every named individual, and not simply the primary veteran applicants. The pension records are presently available for free on Fold3’s website, and are being added to the National Archives catalog on a rolling basis.

According to recent reports, correction 11/20/26 9:30 a.m. EST: A previous version of this article incorrectly stated the pension archive contained around 7 million files. This was based on an initial assessment from researchers in 2010. The article has been updated to reflect the more accurate tally.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Social media influencers claim that having a “ferritin face” may indicate you’re low in iron.

In a recent development, ferritin is a protein that helps your body store iron. You need iron in order to make healthy red blood cells, which carry oxygen from your lungs to the rest of your body. Iron is also crucial for bone marrow, organs, healthy muscles, and brain development.

As “ferritin face” makes its way across social media platforms, owners are describing several tell-tale signs, including:.

It has been revealed that consumers have also shared images of their face before and after taking iron supplements or getting an iron infusion. Videos about “ferritin face” have garnered millions of views on various platforms.

However, medical professionals state that your appearance alone is not enough to diagnose iron deficiency.

According to recent reports, “It’s important to understand that ferritin face is not a medical diagnosis, nor is it a confirmed symptom of iron deficiency. While some people with iron deficiency can appear pale due to low hemoglobin levels in their red blood cells, there are many other symptoms to consider,” remarked Daniel Atkinson, a general practitioner in the United Kingdom and clinical lead at Treated.

It has been revealed that “Notably, these symptoms are also present in many different conditions, and their presence does not necessarily mean iron deficiency anemia or even low ferritin levels. Similar features are seen in people with iron processing and absorption complications, such as gluten intolerance, or in urgent sudden blood loss scenarios,” added Jonathan Jennings, MD, board certified internist at Medical Offices of Manhattan.

Iron deficiency can affect your skin and appearance. These signs are often subtle, but may include:.

In some ways, the social media videos are correct. Your skin and face can change when your iron levels are low.

In a recent development, “The facial signs people point to, like pale skin and a washed-out look, mostly come from anaemia, when your haemoglobin has dropped. But iron deficiency and anaemia aren’t the same thing,” stated Thom Phillips, a general practitioner in the United Kingdom and Chief Medical Officer at Forth. “By the time low iron reveals on your face, your stores are usually close to empty.”.

It is notable to speak with a healthcare professional, who will run blood tests such as a complete blood count and ferritin levels.

It is also important not to take iron supplements without first checking with your healthcare professional, because having too much iron in your body can also cause negative effects.

Too little and too much iron could raise your risk of infection, which is why it’s important not to take supplements without medical supervision.

According to recent reports, the signs and symptoms of iron deficiency can depend on whether you are anemic or not. Some of the early signs may include:.

“These symptoms typically occur because your body produces fewer red blood cells, which results in less oxygen being delivered throughout your body, making you feel tired and weak,” mentioned Atkinson.

Less common symptoms may include:.

While your facial appearance can be a sign that something isn’t right, healthcare professionals consider other symptoms and how you feel overall.

They also rely on blood tests to confirm the diagnosis and guide treatment.

“The misinformation is the idea that you can spot it yourself. That leads to two problems: people with low iron who look fine assume they’re OK, and people who look tired start taking iron supplements they don’t need,” said Phillips.

Atkinson also noted that factors such as different settings and environmental conditions can affect how your face appears.

That being remarked, the “ferritin face” trend may help bring awareness to certain symptoms and when to get them checked.

“[This] trend may raise some awareness about iron deficiency anemia and how low iron levels can impact daily life,” stated Atkinson.

“Fatigue and lightheadedness are common side effects of low iron, but it manifests in other ways too, such as paler skin or increased hair shedding, which can be concerning for many people. If you experience these symptoms, you should let your doctor know so they can help treat the condition appropriately,” he said.

Tesla FSD approved in Italy, the first significant EU market to say yes

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (914 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Italy’s transport ministry has granted provisional approval to Tesla Assisted Driving, the name Tesla now uses for “Full Self-Driving (Supervised)” in Europe.
  • According to recent reports, it also didn’t wait for Brussels.
  • In a recent development, deputy Prime Minister and Transport Minister Matteo Salvini confirmed the decision on X on Friday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Italy’s transport ministry has granted provisional approval to Tesla Assisted Driving, the name Tesla now uses for “Full Self-Driving (Supervised)” in Europe. Italy becomes the 12th European country to allow the system, and the first of the EU’s big markets.

According to recent reports, it also didn’t wait for Brussels. The EU committee that decides on bloc-wide recognition isn’t expected to vote until December at the earliest.

In a recent development, deputy Prime Minister and Transport Minister Matteo Salvini confirmed the decision on X on Friday. He wrote that the ministry (MIT) gave the green light after a “thorough technical feasibility check,” and that Italy is getting ahead of the EU recognition process, which he described as “still being defined.”.

Tesla Europe followed with a one-liner, “Now approved in Italy, rollout begins soon,” and a video of one of its cars driving itself through Rome. There’s no firm rollout date yet.

Recent findings suggest that it’s still a Level 2 driver-assist system. It can steer, brake, accelerate, and handle intersections and lane changes, but the driver has to supervise at all times and stays fully responsible for the car.

The Dutch vehicle authority RDW was first, approving FSD Supervised on April 10 under Article 39 of the EU type-approval regulation. Other member states can then recognize that approval nationally, one by one.

Ten did before Italy: Belgium, Croatia, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Latvia, Lithuania, Slovakia, and Slovenia. Those are mostly small markets. Together with the Netherlands, they add up to about 70 million people, or roughly 15% of the EU’s population.

Italy alone has about 59 million people, so Friday’s decision nearly doubles the share of Europeans who can legally use the system, to close to 30%.

Recent findings suggest that rome’s position moved fast. In April, Senator Carlo Calenda formally asked Salvini’s ministry to prioritize the approval. On October 29, Salvini posted that he’d had a “very positive and constructive” call with Elon Musk and that Italy supported a “swift EU approval,” which read at the time as backing for an EU-level decision, not a national one. Three weeks later, Italy went national.

A lot changed in between. Tesla dropped the “Full Self-Driving” name in Europe after Germany’s Transport Ministry called it misleading, and cut the maximum speed margin from 50% to 10% over the limit. Then on November 16, the RDW approved stricter driver monitoring, including hands on the wheel above 130 km/h. That’s the version Italy is approving.

The EU’s Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles (TCMV) pushed the Tesla vote to December after holding only discussions in October. Bloc-wide approval needs a qualified majority: at least 15 of 27 member states, representing at least 65% of the EU population.

Germany mentioned in October it would back approval after Tesla agreed to the rename and the speed cap. If it follows through, Germany and the 12 approving countries would cover roughly 47% of the EU’s population.

That’s progress for Tesla, but it’s not 65%. France refused a national approval in July, and Spain hasn’t recognized the Dutch approval. Tesla needs at least one of them, plus most of the remaining holdouts.

Recent findings suggest that I used FSD for five days this past week. It's impressive on controlled roads.

Even in Chill driving mode, there were still more than a few times that I had to use the Critical feedback.

To think it will ever be perfect is pure fantasy. I will never climb into a automobile that does not have steering controls.

Seven repairs and $10,000 on a leaky roof in two years, with no guarantees. When you factor in Musk, I'm done.

Both Carmax and OnlyUsedTesla acknowledged receiving my requests. No offers from either service 48-hours later. Guess I'm not the only one that's done with Tesla.

This is a real win for Tesla, and for Italian owners with HW4 cars who have been paying for a feature they couldn’t use at home. Italy is Tesla’s first substantial European market to say yes, and it shifts momentum going into December.

But it’s pretty crazy that now Europe is going to get a safer FSD than in the US.

I bet that this will get reflected in the data, if we ever get to see it.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • If you're tired of feeling like you're never quite enough, or that you're never going to get "there" (wherever there is), consider the following questions.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.

If you're tired of feeling like you're never quite enough, or that you're never going to get "there" (wherever there is), consider the following questions.

Instead of skimming through these questions the way you might read a typical blog post, I'd like to suggest that you wait until you have a quiet moment. Sit or lie down. Read the words silently or out loud, and really consider them. Try them on, the way you might try on a piece of clothing to see how they fit.

Sources indicate that notice what happens inside your body as you read. See if any of these ideas can sink in. If they can't right now, that's OK, too.

Sometimes old programming runs deep and can feel hard to change. With patience and practice, old beliefs can be questioned and updated, and newly introduced ways of thinking and being can take root.

So get comfortable, take a slow, deep breath, and consider these possibilities.

What if I remembered that self-critical thoughts aren't necessarily facts, and I didn't have to believe everything I think?

What if I could begin choosing fresh thoughts and beliefs that are kinder, more supportive, and actually feel good?

What if I got off my own back, got on my own side, and decided that I am a good person doing the best I can?

What if I remembered that kindness, compassion, and encouragement help people grow, while berating, pressure, and perfectionism often get in the way?

What if my worth didn't depend on how much I accomplished, how productive I was, or how well I did things?

What if I allowed myself to do things imperfectly, and let good enough be good enough?

What if I could let myself be a beginner, make mistakes, change my mind, and learn as I go, rather than expecting myself to get everything right every time?

What if I spent less time living in worst-case scenarios about the future and more time in the present moment?

What if I slowed down, ever so slightly, and sprinkled small moments of conscious breathing and quiet awareness throughout my day?

What if I stepped out of the never-ending race to get somewhere and spent more moments in actual, factual reality?

What if I softened my gaze when I looked at myself and softened my thoughts when I thought about myself?

What if I spent less time comparing myself to others, remembering that I know nothing about what their lives actually feel like on the inside, and instead offered myself more moments of grace?

What if I became curious about what enoughness feels like?

Sources indicate that what if I decided that, in this exact moment, I am already enough? I can still do what I'm moved to do, pursue what matters to me, and take care of what needs to be done without staying trapped on the endless treadmill of never-enoughness.

What if I simply said, Thank you for what I have, kept the welcome mat out, and stayed open to whatever comes next?

What if, just for today, I let myself be enough?

Turn off reality TV and turn on the bald eagle cams. It’s all the drama you need.

In a recent development, when internet-famous bald eagle Shadow seemingly welcomed a mysterious new female into his nest earlier this week, many fans have questioned the whereabouts of Kaydee. After the death of Shadow’s longtime partner Jackie in August, he had been spotted spending time with the 4-year-old banded female eagle named KD1 (later renamed Kaydee). It seemed like the eagles might head into mating season as a pair, but after the arrival of a new, large female, it’s unclear how the relationships will all shake out.

According to recent reports, since the appearance of the mystery female, nicknamed Big Beautiful Visitor or BBV by some fans, Kaydee has disappeared from view of Friends of Big Bear Valley (FOBBV)’s two cameras. She was last spotted by the cameras on November 14 in the Roost Tree, according to FOBBV. Despite concerns that she may be injured or had left the area, wildlife photographers have continued to document Kaydee’s presence near Big Bear Lake as recently as November 18.

Photographer Alla Shumko shared photos of Kaydee perched near Massive Bear Lake on November 18. Kaydee’s double bands are visible as she observed a scuffle between younger eagles fighting over fish.

In a recent development, mating season is well underway, so viewers of FOBBV’s 24/7 livecams have been watching closely for signs that Shadow has selected a new partner. Shadow has worked with both Kaydee and the new eagle on nest maintenance and shared “beaky kisses” with each female, both signs of bonding in bald eagles. Bald eagle mating involves a bit of aerial acrobatics—copulating pairs can be seen in what’s called a “cartwheel display,” in which they lock talons in mid-air while tumbling down to the ground. Male eagles do not have an external phallus, so mating occurs via a touch of cloacas. Vocalizations can typically be heard during the act, which lasts about 7 to 12 seconds, according to Raptor Resource.

Recent findings suggest that as this is nature, we humans can’t predict or influence who Shadow will pick as a newly introduced partner. Or if he picks at all. All we can do is watch and wait and let nature take its course.

  • The GTI Rabbit Edition also boasts the first North American use of Dark Moss Green Metallic, a paint job previously reserved for Europe’s Golf GTI Edition 50 that set the front-wheel drive Nurburgring lap record.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that mid-year model automobiles are like safeties in football games: rare, but maybe not as uncommon as you might guess at first. But the latest in that tradition, the 2027.5 Volkswagen GTI Rabbit Edition, doesn’t just split the difference between 2027 and 2028; it also slides between the S and SE models that make up the lower tiers of the lineup, while bringing along some of the sweet features from the top-shelf GTI Autobahn trim. In other words, it has the makings of a Goldilocks special.

Recent findings suggest that first, a dash of history. “Rabbit” was the name originally used by VW for the Golf in the U.S. and Canadian markets back in the days of the Mk1, including on the first GTI that arrived in 1979 in the Great White North and in ‘83 in the States. (The tech giant then returned to the Rabbit name for the Mk5 Golf here, but that’s less consequential—or memorable.) In honor of that first GTI, this new trim includes an adorable little chrome bunny on its hatch, in addition to blacked-out mirror caps, grille, and other trim bits scattered around the exterior that replace red items on other members of the current GTI family.

The GTI Rabbit Edition also boasts the first North American use of Dark Moss Green Metallic, a paint job previously reserved for Europe’s Golf GTI Edition 50 that set the front-wheel drive Nurburgring lap record. The 19-inch black wheels come from the Golf R, and are wrapped as standard in summer performance tires, versus the all-season rubber that normally comes with less-expensive GTIs. But the most notable change on the fun side is the presence of the DCC adaptive dampers, for which you otherwise would have to spring for the top-shelf Autobahn trim to get. Inside, meanwhile, the Rabbit Edition picks up the GTI SE’s GTI Clubsport ArtVelours material on its comfy yet supportive front buckets and rear bench.

Like all other current GTIs, unfortunately, the Rabbit Edition forces buyers to use a seven-speed dual-clutch automatic to change the gears tied to its 241-horsepower turbocharged inline-four; the manual gearbox remains locked in the past. Still, if you can look past that, the Rabbit Edition has the makings of a steal. Volkswagen hasn’t announced pricing yet—that’ll come closer to its on-sale date of Q2 2027—but seeing as how the carmaker is quite explicit about where it lands in the lineup, expect it to come in the $36,250 of the GTI S and the $40,240 of the GTI SE, plus or minus any little price bumps they might pick up in the next half model year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’ve been paying any attention to the shooter market these past few months, you won’t be surprised to learn that Battlefield 6 has been an unprecedented success for EA, and the Battlefield series as a whole.

In a recent development, the game managed to sell over 7 million units at launch, climbing to the top of the charts anywhere you look, including setting new series concurrent player records on Steam. Thanks to new data, we now better understand the true scale of this launch.

Sources indicate that the latest Circana report, which looks at game and hardware sales in the United States, has arrived. This iteration covers the month of October, which is when Battlefield 6 was released.

Sources indicate that battlefield 6 was the top-selling game across all platforms during October - which isn’t surprising. It has overtaken NBA 2K26 to become 2025’s best-selling game year-to-date, making it the best-selling Battlefield game ever.

In October alone, the game sold more than the lifetime sales of Battlefield 1, previously the best-selling entry in the franchise.

Sources indicate that battlefield 6 even set records beyond just its own series, having now produced the highest single-month dollar sales (physical and digital) total for any full game released in the last three years. The previous record holder was 2022’s Modern Warfare 2.

According to recent reports, november’s report, which is set to arrive midway through December, will show, once and for all, whether Battlefield 6 has been able to overtake Black Ops 7. With one exception, Call of Duty games have, for more than a decade, topped the best-selling year-to-date chart. Regardless of the quality of the individual titles, or the competition in any given year, nothing has been able to shake that dominance.

Given all this momentum, Battlefield 6 has a shot at dethroning Call of Duty this year, beating Black Ops 7 to become the year’s best-seller. You never want to count out the sheer popularity of Call of Duty among casual players, however, which is what’s going to make December’s report all the more interesting.

The fresh Renault Twingo E-Tech is among the most affordable vehicles, electric or gas-powered, starting at just £14,745 in the UK, or under $20,000.

Another affordable, practical EV the US will never see. Renault’s new Twingo E-Tech is an electric remake of its iconic 1990s city car.

The retro-looking EV went on sale in Europe earlier this year, starting at under €20,000 ($22,000), before government incentives. In places like Germany, it starts at about €13,990 ($15,500), including the €6,000 ($6,600) federal EV grant.

In the UK, Renault revealed that prices for the Twingo E-Tech will start at just £14,745, or about $19,500. That includes the government’s Electric Clean Car Grant (ECG) of £3,750 ($4,900).

At that price, Renault’s new electric car is among the most affordable vehicles available, including gas-powered cars.

It’s cheaper than the gas-powered Dacia Sandero (£14,765) and BYD’s cheapest EV, the Dolphin Surf (£18,675). Only a few cars are lower-priced, including the Dacia Spring (£11,990) and Leapmotor T03 (£12,995).

What do you get for the price? At just 3,790 mm (149.2″) long, the electric city car is a bit smaller than the Hyundai Inster and the BYD Dolphin Surf.

For those in the US, that’s even smaller than the first-generation Chevy Bolt EV, which measured 4,145 mm (163.2″) in length.

Despite its compact size, the “cheeky, practical” 5-door city car, as Renault calls it, offers up to 360 liters of boot capacity. It also features independent, sliding 50/50 folding rear seats to haul bigger items like a surfboard.

With up to 50 kW DC fast charging, Renault said the Twingo E-Tech can charge from 15% to 80% in 28 minutes.

The base Renault Twingo E-Tech Evolution, priced from £14,745 ($19,500), uses a 27.5 kWh LFP battery and an 80 hp (60 kW) motor, delivering up to 163 miles of WLTP range.

The entry-level version features 16″ steel wheels, a 7″ driver display, 10″ navigation screen, and ADAS features, including cruise control and lane-keep assist.

Renault will offer three Twingo E-Tech trims in total. The mid-range Techno trim gains 18″ wheels, Google built-in with Renault’s Reno avatar, a reversing camera, automatic climate control, a hands-free key card, One Pedal driving, and heated front seats. It starts at £16,245 ($21,500), including the £3,750 ($4,900) ECG.

With Google built in, drivers can easily find and navigate to charging stations via Google Maps, use Google Gemini AI virtual assistance, or access over 100 apps, including Waze and Amazon Music.

Sources indicate that at least this car has some styling unlike the generic box style VW offerings in this category. In this size car I prefer the SUV style of the Dacia Spring for myself, but of course we will never see any of these wonderful cars in the USA.

The top-spec Twingo E-Tech Launch Edition, priced from £17,645 ($23,200), including the £3,750 ($4,900) ECG, adds a suite of ADAS features, including blind-spot warning, rear cross-traffic alert and hands-free parking.

Inside, the Launch Edition features a special mottled textile upholstery with red stitching and premium floor mats.

Renault is offering a special promo for those who buy a new Twingo E-Tech through Mobilize Financial Services on a PCP or HP agreement by June 30, 2027, which includes two years’ free servicing.

Interested buyers can purchase the Twingo R Pass for £100, giving them priority access to ordering, a mini Twingo E-Tech model, and a green Renault key cover.

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (462 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Less than 400 adult North Atlantic right whales (Eubalaena glacialis) still exist in the wild, making them one of the world’s most critically endangered species.
  • “Naming right whales is a fun and creative activity for our research community, but it also allows an opportunity to connect with the whales on an individual level,” Amy Warren, an aquarium scientific program officer and name project coordinator, mentioned in Anderson Cabot Center’s announcement.
  • The 2026 inductees also include Grand Slam (Catalog #3991) and Slide (Catalog #4991).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Less than 400 adult North Atlantic right whales (Eubalaena glacialis) still exist in the wild, making them one of the world’s most critically endangered species. Of those, 20 have officially received spiffy latest names from conservationists at the New England Aquarium’s Anderson Cabot Center for Ocean Life. The researchers curate the annual North Atlantic Right Whale Catalog, and attach personable monikers to a select few baleen cetaceans in order to more easily monitor them. This year, it’s time to wave hello to Dodo, Volcano, and Dolly.

“Naming right whales is a fun and creative activity for our research community, but it also allows an opportunity to connect with the whales on an individual level,” Amy Warren, an aquarium scientific program officer and name project coordinator, mentioned in Anderson Cabot Center’s announcement. “It can be hard to relate to Catalog #5299, but a whale named Nibbles is bound to be memorable.”.

The 2026 inductees also include Grand Slam (Catalog #3991) and Slide (Catalog #4991). The sister whales have a mother named Fenway (Catalog #2791), who was also named in honor of the Boston Red Sox. Grand Slam earned her new name thanks to her three patches of raised tissue known as callosities that resemble the bases on a baseball field. Meanwhile, Slide received their name due to the curved scar on her back that recalls someone sliding through home plate. Other right whale names this year include Goose, Donegal, and even Gonzo for the beloved Muppet.

“Although the names are intended to help researchers at sea, they also give the general public a better understanding of the individual whales,” added Caroline Mowdy, a spokesperson for Whale and Dolphin Conservation (WDC).

According to recent reports, collaborators at the WDC also created some lighthearted, yearbook-esque biographies for each whale. For example, Dolly (Catalog #4191), whose callosity looks strikingly similar to the late, great country singer’s larger-than-life hair, apparently loves the song, “Jolene.” Then again, who doesn’t?

It has been revealed that “We see these whales and their families grow each year,” said Mowdy. “Knowing them makes the tragedies even more tragic, but it also makes our determination to protect them even stronger.”.

According to recent reports, on Monday, the North Atlantic Right Whale Consortium declared that there are roughly 382 North Atlantic right whales, representing a 1.8 percent drop in population size from the 2024 estimate. Their primary threats remain getting tangled in fishing line and vessel strikes.

However, even amid their struggles, the 2025–2026 right whale calving season saw the most calves born since 2009. A total of 24 calves were born, including a surprising late addition that was spotted in Canada in September.

Mammograms May Offer Early Insight Into Cardiovascular Disease

📅 08 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (818 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mammograms are widely used to help detect breast cancer, but they may also offer insight into heart health.
  • The routine X-ray screening may identify breast arterial calcification (BAC), which is the presence of calcium deposits within the walls of the small arteries in the breast.
  • On a mammogram, BAC is commonly identified as thin, white, parallel lines that give a “tram-track” appearance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mammograms are widely used to help detect breast cancer, but they may also offer insight into heart health.

The routine X-ray screening may identify breast arterial calcification (BAC), which is the presence of calcium deposits within the walls of the small arteries in the breast.

On a mammogram, BAC is commonly identified as thin, white, parallel lines that give a “tram-track” appearance.

Industry observers note that while BAC is harmless to the breasts, it is associated with a significantly higher risk of cardiovascular disease. A 2022 study found women with BAC were 51% more likely to develop heart disease or experience a stroke than those without it.

Laxmi Mehta, MD, a cardiologist at The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center, said BAC is associated with cardiovascular risk factors, such as diabetes, high blood pressure, and high cholesterol. Additionally, BAC has been connected to:.

“The reasons for BAC resulting in higher risks for cardiovascular disease are not definitely determined; however, there are some potential mechanisms, one being that they share similar risk factors that result in vascular injury or metabolic stress that result in vascular calcification and atherosclerosis,” Mehta told Healthline.

Cheng-Han Chen, MD, interventional cardiologist and medical director of the Structural Heart Program at MemorialCare Saddleback Medical Center, added that because BAC and heart disease share many of the same risk factors, “calcium in breast arteries therefore suggests disease in the heart (coronary) and brain arteries as well,” he told Healthline.

While 1 in 39 females in the United States dies from breast cancer each year, cardiovascular disease causes one out of every three deaths, resulting in 1 death per minute.

“Cardiovascular disease is still the most common cause of death in premenopausal women,” Richard Reitherman, MD, PhD, a radiologist and medical director of breast imaging at MemorialCare Breast Center at Orange Coast Medical Center, told Healthline.

“The presentation of cardiovascular disease in premenopausal women is notoriously different than in postmenopausal women, primarily [because] there are no typical symptoms such as chest pain.”.

Reitherman remarked that a prevalent and common health screening procedure such as a mammogram can lead to the early identification of women with silent cardiovascular disease.

“Cardiovascular outcome studies that have included breast arterial calcifications as a risk factor are increasingly reported in the medical literature,” he said.

“The hope is that identifying younger women with silent cardiovascular risks [like BAC along with] appropriate integrated risk identification, analysis, and interventions can significantly reduce mortality in this age group.”.

Mehta said there are several reasons BAC has been overlooked as a risk factor for heart disease.

“Mammograms are completed for assessment of breast cancer, and BAC has been historically an ‘incidental’ finding, which is not clinically relevant from an oncologic standpoint,” she said.

Additionally, there is no standardization on quantification of BAC severity, nor is it a required component of mammogram reports, said Mehta.

However, routine reporting of BAC on mammograms is an urgent goal of the American College of Radiology, Society of Breast Imaging, and Medicare, said Reitherman.

In fact, it is gaining traction in the United States. A new Maryland law, passed on October 1, requires mammography centers to notify women when a BAC is detected on their mammogram.

“Automated identification and reporting of these calcifications detected on screening mammograms will become increasingly prevalent in the coming months [and] years,” stated Reitherman.

The next step is to identify this group of women to primary care physicians so that appropriate risk evaluation can take place, Reitherman added.

In addition to doctors routinely screening for conditions related to heart disease, such as diabetes, high blood pressure, and high cholesterol, he hopes BAC will also be routinely considered.

“Under current development are protocols to identify patients needing a cardiologist’s training and expertise to appropriately stratify this group of patients,” remarked Reitherman.

“The common healthcare behavior [of] having regular mammograms not only reduces risk of morbidity and mortality from breast cancer but will hopefully contribute to the reduction of morbidity and mortality from cardiovascular disease in younger women.”.

He said this type of integrated healthcare approach demonstrates cross-specialty integration and coordination among women, radiologists, and their healthcare providers to improve women’s lives.

“This is an amazing game-changing opportunity,” Reitherman noted.

Mehta stated it’s reasonable for women to ask if BAC is present on their mammogram report.

“But if it is not uniformly reported by the radiologist, the individual clinician may not have the answer,” she noted.

More research is needed before BAC on mammograms can be used routinely to predict heart disease.

Finding out your BAC could provide additional information to help you and your doctors decide how aggressively to address your cardiovascular risk factors, Chen noted.

It has been revealed that reitherman agreed. “The goal of reducing morbidity and mortality from any cause such as cardiovascular disease is based on recognition of risk factors, followed by appropriate lifestyle and pharmacologic interventions,” he remarked.

#98267. 'So No One Told You Life Was Gonna Be This Way'

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (765 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Psychologytoday ↗ Open Full Page

'So No One Told You Life Was Gonna Be This Way'

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (765 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.
  • Showing up for friends on their good days is easy.
  • In a recent development, this month, Marsha Linehan, developer of DBT, died.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.

Showing up for friends on their good days is easy. You can celebrate their wins and enjoy their happiness. But being there, really being present for friends when they’re having a rough day or when they do dumb things, that can be more challenging. Our friend is upset, so they spend too much money, or they’re worried, so they pull out of something they had to do, or they’re angry, so they break things. How do we validate their emotions without endorsing their choices?

So, No One Told You Life Was Gonna Be This Way.

In a recent development, this month, Marsha Linehan, developer of DBT, died. One of her many contributions to the psychology world was how to validate emotions with precision. She described six levels of how to validate emotions. The aim is to validate with the highest level possible, but different situations will require different levels. At all times, the goal is to help people notice that their emotion is valid and welcome, even if you don’t agree with the behavior that follows. Your friend doesn’t need a lecture after they’ve done something wrong; they want to feel emotionally understood.

Recent findings suggest that the most basic level is to simply stay awake and pay attention. I say "simply," but in these days of constant distractions, and phones and devices trying to hold our focus, even just being fully present can be a challenge. How can you show your friend that you’re really listening? You can use eye contact, nodding, asking questions, saying "uh-huh," and more.

The second level is accurate reflection. When you paraphrase back what they’ve said, you let them know that you’ve understood what they’re saying, especially the emotion they’re trying to communicate. Do this without criticism or advice, even if you don’t agree with everything they’ve said. Validation isn’t approval of behavior; it’s letting them know that their feelings are welcome.

Level three is reflecting the unarticulated parts. Let them know that you’ve understood even the aspects they haven’t explicitly told you. Name emotions that you’re guessing they’re probably feeling, e.g., "Oh my gosh, you must have been so hurt by him saying that." It doesn’t even matter if you guess the right emotion. If they reply, "Actually, I was more angry than sad," then you still have lots of emotion to validate.

At the fourth level, you are validating using past history or biology. Letting your friend know that their behavior makes sense based on their life so far. Statements like "After all you’ve been through this year, I get why this would feel so painful" can put context to their uncomfortable emotions. Even if you would have felt differently in the same situation, you are able to validate their emotion because you understand that their road to this point has been different from yours.

In a recent development, even more powerful than that is normalising the emotion. Letting your friend know that anyone in that situation would probably feel the same way. Saying things like "I get so upset when that happens," or "That’s something that worries me too," or "We all have moments like that." We can normalise the emotion, even when the behavior wasn’t something we agree with. We can understand that when we’re upset, we make choices that aren’t always the most helpful, and the emotion is still valid. Also, you can normalize their emotion without launching into your own similar story; if your friend is upset, they need you to listen to their pain.

In a recent development, finally, the highest level of validation is radical genuineness. You listen to them describe their experiences, and you respond with genuine emotion. You're not patronising and saying "there, there." Instead, you are moved by their situation, and you care about them. This is demonstrated through words, body language, and emotion.

Validating your friends (or partner or family member) with the highest level of validation that feels appropriate for the situation is what will help you wholeheartedly be there for them when they’re broke, their job’s a joke, or their love life’s DOA.

It has been revealed that koerner, K. (2012). Doing dialectical behavior therapy: A practical guide. The Guilford Press.

Industry observers note that linehan, M. M. (1993). Cognitive-behavioral treatment of borderline personality disorder. Guilford Press.

Linehan, M. M. (2020). Building a life worth living: A memoir. Random House.

Max Verstappen, who held provisional pole until the final flurry of attempts, will inherit the P1 starting spot, and George Russell will start second after qualifying third.

Russell, by far the fastest in Friday’s practice, asked the Mercedes pit wall if he could have a tow, knowing Mercedes was the clear frontrunner and his champion teammate was destined to start further back in the field.

Mercedes didn’t oblige, and both drivers entered the waiting game with the rest of the contenders, as no one wanted to be the first driver out for the final lap, punching through the frigid cold air of the Las Vegas desert alone.

Ultimately, Verstappen went first and did not improve on his first Q3 time, which was still good enough for an elevated front-row starting spot. Antonelli crossed the line to start his lap with a second remaining.

Industry observers note that lando Norris will start third after qualifying fourth ahead of Isack Hadjar and Arvid Lindblad. Oscar Piastri found himself in a familiar starting position of seventh but faces a 10-place grid penalty.

With rain on Thursday and a dry forecast for every session of consequence during the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend, most contenders first saw what their fresh 2027 cars had during FP3 on Friday, ahead of qualifying.

Neither Ferrari made it to Q3, settling for 11th and 12th as neither Lewis Hamilton nor Charles Leclerc put themselves in position to give the other a tow.

Nico Hulkenberg, Carlos Sainz, Gabriel Bortoleto, and Alex Albon were knocked out in Q2.

Haas reserve driver Rafael Camara nearly made it to Q2 in his second F1 qualifying attempt but was knocked out at the last minute by the Audis. He joined Sergio Perez, Fernando Alonso, Lance Stroll, Valtteri Bottas, and Ollie Bearman.
